audience: Jay is the primary reader; his dad, with whom he makes grant and investment decisions and who is the final decision-maker, is second. Other readers include individual activists and people in the vegan movement and alternative protein sector. Do not assume every reader is a grantmaker.
purpose: Help Jay do his work better: assess organizations and individuals with limited evidence, ask better due-diligence questions, structure grants (including matching grants), and consider whether other funders would fund the work anyway. Understand alternative protein consumer demand, especially among non-vegans, commercial viability, investment conditions, and decisions affecting existing holdings. Discover useful AI tools and techniques and understand broader AI developments, including the world of potential future movement donors working in AI. Never expose private portfolio information in newsletter copy.
voice: Concise, professional, engaging, skeptical but fair. Cohesive short narratives, with researchers and organizations explicitly identified and source links woven into the prose. No formulaic bold labels, intro, greeting, closing, or explicit reading-time label. Polished warm magazine appearance inspired by Axios, with serif headlines and muted green accents.
selection: Global coverage, selected by consequence, evidence, and relevance. No geographic preference, topic quotas, fixed order, or minimum story count. A few substantial stories plus short updates on busy days. Prefer a tighter briefing even if marginal developments are omitted. Apply the same significance threshold to organizations and companies Jay has supported as to everyone else. Consequential firsthand announcements qualify with clear attribution even without independent corroboration.
freshness: Every story must be anchored in a verified new development within the reporting window. Older material is dated context only. A newly released evaluation of an older intervention can qualify as new evidence; an old evaluation discovered today cannot.
analysis: Explain relevance with concrete reasoning and material qualifications integrated into the narrative. Identify who did research; distinguish organizational claims from independent findings. Questions readers could ask are welcome when useful; do not assume every reader is a funder or force action items. Consider intervention effectiveness, counterfactual funding, grant design, consumer adoption and financial conditions where supported. Distinguish reported results from interpretation. Brief commentary on each of five daily charts is included in the total reading budget; describe measured changes, avoid unsupported causal stories, and identify stale or monthly observations honestly.

topics.Alternative Protein: Consequential global developments in plant-based, cultivated and fermentation-derived foods: non-vegan consumer acceptance, repeat purchase, price and taste, commercialization, investment, financing and restructuring, company performance, science and policy. Regular interest in vegan pet food. Animal-free materials such as leather: major developments only. Apply the same significance threshold to all companies.
topics.Vegan Movement: Consequential global animal advocacy, plant-based adoption, nonprofit effectiveness, intervention evaluations, policy and campaigns. Regular interest in plant-based nutrition and human health, sanctuaries and direct animal care, and philanthropy or grantmaking research outside animal advocacy when lessons could apply. Alternatives to animal testing: major developments only. FAST is an email list, not an organization. Its material may be quoted, paraphrased, and attributed without special limits, but never included in public search queries. Religious giving and unrelated charity are not newsletter interests merely because Jay funds them.
topics.AI: Important AI developments broadly: research and capabilities, industry, policy, safety, security, major incidents and societal effects, as well as tools and techniques useful at work. AI merits coverage on its own significance. Understanding people and organizations in AI, including Anthropic, can help connect with potential future donors to animal causes; do not speculate about individuals’ wealth, sympathy or giving, and do not force animal-advocacy connections. Skip routine hype and minor updates.
